evidence: Sen. Ep. 38.1: hoc inter nōs epistulārum commercium frequentāre (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Commercium is trade, and so any give and take: of letters, the correspondence itself (Traupman 297, epistulārum commercium, correspondence).

evidence: Cic. Fam. 1.7.1; Att. 6.1.24 (Lewis & Short, s.v. colloquor)
terms.comment: Cicero’s way of putting it: a letter is a conversation with an absent friend.
For the single letter, and with crēbrō or saepe for a correspondence kept up (see contact).

phrases.latin: tū, quaesō, crēbrō ad mē scrībe vel quod in buccam vēnerit
phrases.english: please write to me often, even whatever comes into your head

phrases.latin: hoc inter nōs epistulārum commercium frequentāre
phrases.english: to keep up this exchange of letters between us
